target_customer: Software companies and developers building end-to-end encrypted apps, including crypto and Web3 apps, that need user key recovery
problem: Zero-knowledge and end-to-end encrypted apps lose user data when a password or seed phrase is lost. Bunkyr offers a hardware-secured API so apps can offer a familiar recovery path without seeing user data.
business_model: Developer API sold to application companies (B2B SaaS)
product_category: Developer security API, encrypted key recovery

competitors.name: Torus
competitors.what: Key management for crypto using distributed key generation so a key can be reassembled from node shards
competitors.funding_then: 2M USD seed led by Multicoin Capital, July 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining hardware-secured key storage with zero-knowledge guarantees and a developer API is hard cryptographic engineering for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Security trust and integration into customers' encryption flows create switching costs, but no patents or traction data were found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying Bunkyr.

market_need_then: The YC description argues zero-knowledge architectures are the safeguard against breaches but impose heavy UX and engineering burdens; seed phrase loss was a known pain in crypto wallets around 2021 to 2022.

branding.domain_note: Uses bunkyr.com; the domain did not resolve from this research environment, which may be a network restriction rather than a dead site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain developer security language: no seed phrases or backup codes

brand_strength.rationale: Little public brand material or press about the brand was found, and the spelling is confusable with Bunkr and Bunker, other companies.

outcome_analysis: Bunkyr is a YC Winter 2022 company that raised a 1M USD pre-seed in June 2022 for a zero-knowledge key recovery API. The YC page lists it as active, but no later rounds, customers or exit were found, so the outcome is unresolved and little can be said about why it has or has not progressed.
notes: Founders not named on the YC page or the sources opened, so the list is empty rather than guessed. Pre-seed of 1M USD seen at fintech.global and in search snippets for CB Insights, CoinCarp and StartupIntros (dates June 1, 16 or 20; amounts agree). CB Insights total of 1.5M is unverified. Investor lists differ by source; only fintech.global names were recorded. Lit Protocol raised 13M in September 2022, after the batch, and is not listed as a founding competitor. bunkyr.com could not be fetched (host did not resolve in this environment). An unrelated BUNKR run by Kurt Long appeared in branding searches and was not treated as this company.
